Bug_Title: Expressions used in "assert" should not produce side effects
Bug_Details:
Since assert statements aren’t executed by default (they must be enabled with JVM flags) developers should never rely on their
execution the evaluation of any logic required for correct program function.
Noncompliant code example
assert myList.remove(myList.get(0));  // Noncompliant
Compliant solution
boolean removed = myList.remove(myList.get(0));
assert removed;
Bug_Explanation: The 'assert' statement is used to verify that a certain condition is true at runtime. If the condition is false, the assert statement throws an AssertionError. In this code, the 'assert' statement is used to check if an element from the list was successfully removed. This is a bug because the evaluation of the'remove' method call is used as an argument to the 'assert' statement. This can cause side effects because the'remove' method is called twice - once as an argument to the 'assert' statement and again as part of the code that uses the 'assert' statement.
